leverage.exposure: None. No leveraged position exists and none is being opened. Both offers together sit just inside the balance, so in every possible resolution order — either one clearing, both clearing, neither clearing — the balance ends positive. That matters more than anything else on this page, because a negative balance when the matchday starts scores zero for the entire matchday. The hard ceiling for any further bidding while the Leipzig offer is live is the balance minus that offer, and the standing offer on the Frankfurt midfielder is already sitting just under it. Nothing may be bid above that line without a sale landing first, and no sale is legal at the current squad size.

binding_gap: Still the third attacker, and it is still unfixed. With only two attackers the squad can fill exactly one formation, and that formation forces a midfielder with no points history into the fielded eleven. The live offer on the Leipzig attacker is the fix: it unlocks two further formations, pushes the zero-scorer out of the side, and is by a wide margin the largest single-move gain available on this board. Everything else this run is secondary to whether that offer clears tomorrow afternoon. The second offer, on the Frankfurt midfielder, addresses the follow-on gap — midfield depth behind the one genuine scorer — and would displace the same zero-scorer in the alternative shapes.

verdict.headline: No action.
verdict.detail: No action. Both offers are alive, both are unopposed, and between them they commit essentially the whole balance — so there is nothing to buy, nothing that needs selling, and nothing to raise. The one new fact is that the nightly market-value update landed and moved the ground under the Gomis bid: he repriced upward, which shaved the premium from comfortably above the contested-listing ceiling to sitting exactly on it. That is not a reason to top up while Georg is the only bidder, and the next update falls after both offers resolve, so no further erosion is possible before either clears. Hold both, touch nothing, and let them run.

sell.reason: No sale this run, and that is a structural verdict rather than a judgment about any player. At eleven with exactly one legal formation there are zero spare men, so any sale at all takes the squad to ten and fills no formation — a self-inflicted penalty far larger than anything a sale could bank. The two designated funding sales, the Hoffenheim full-back and the Mainz substitute, both stay on hold for that reason alone. The Hoffenheim full-back's case for selling has actually weakened this run: his valuation turned upward for the first time in days, so the bleed argument that motivated the sale no longer applies with the same force. Both become sellable the moment a twelfth outfield body lands, and only then.

buy.reason: Nothing on the board is buyable, and the reason is arithmetic rather than taste — the two live offers commit almost the entire balance, so the affordable universe is a rounding error wide. Three listings arrived since the last run and all three would be refused even with money in hand: a Gladbach defender with a negative score who would be a sixth defender in a shape that caps at five, a Union Berlin midfielder carrying an explicit non-fit flag on the listing itself, and a Hamburg midfielder also on a negative score. The board's one genuinely good asset, the Leipzig defender at the top of the price range, remains unaffordable in every branch and stays refused for that reason. The two standing offers are the buy list: a Leipzig attacker who starts and creates, which is the move that fixes the formation, and a Frankfurt midfielder who played a full ninety on the opening weekend. Neither needs raising while no one is bidding against them.
